title: KU Leuven Summer of Science

proposed_updates.citizenship_restrictions: None -- explicitly 'open to all high school students,' with Flemish students named only as the 'primary audience,' not the exclusive one.
proposed_updates.cost_currency_note: EUR, not USD. This is the non-Flemish-student rate; Flemish high school students pay a reduced EUR 380. Confirms and freshly re-dates the exact figures already on record as a currency-gap example in summer_schema_and_pipeline_gaps_2026-08-24.md (#1) -- not a new discovery of the number itself, but a fresh confirmation plus the eligibility text that number was missing context for.
proposed_updates.current_cycle_label: 'The application for the 2026 edition is currently closed.' 2027 not yet open (newsletter signup only).

turkey_access_reasoning: Explicit 'open to all high school students' framing with a named (not exclusive) primary audience, plus a real, differentiated non-Flemish fee tier -- this is concrete evidence of an operational non-Belgian applicant pathway, not just silence.

evidence.quote: This summer school is open to all high school students; its primary audience is Flemish high school students. [...] The fee for participation in the KU Leuven Summer of Science 2026 is 380 EUR for students at Flemish high schools, and 430 EUR for other students.

title: NSLC Business & Entrepreneurship
canonical_name: National Student Leadership Conference (NSLC) -- Business & Entrepreneurship
host_institution: Rotates among University of Michigan, Duke University, UC Berkeley, Columbia University

proposed_updates.citizenship_restrictions: None found; a dedicated 'International Students' resource page is maintained separately from the main eligibility text.
proposed_updates.cost_currency_note: USD. Price ladder by host campus: Michigan $4,195 / Duke $4,295 / UC Berkeley $4,295 / Columbia $4,495 for a 9-day residential session, inclusive of housing, meals, and activities.
proposed_updates.current_cycle_label: Rolling admissions -- 'NSLC will continue to accept applications if space is available' beyond suggested seasonal deadlines. No hard cutoff date to record.

turkey_access_reasoning: Explicit international-student eligibility with a dedicated resource page, plus rolling (not date-limited) admissions, which is itself a meaningful accessibility fact for a family in a different time zone/academic calendar planning around a Turkish school year.

evidence.claim: International eligibility, price ladder, rolling admissions
evidence.quote: We encourage all 6th-12th grade students who demonstrate academic excellence and leadership ability to apply [with a dedicated International Students resource page]. [...] University of Michigan: $4,195 [...] Columbia University: $4,495 [...] NSLC will continue to accept applications if space is available.

notes: This is a commercial (Envision-operated) program hosted at rotating university campuses, not a university-official program -- provider_type recorded as 'company' rather than 'university_official' per Contract SS8's provider/host distinction.

title: Northwestern CTD 3-Week Academic Summer Camps
canonical_name: Northwestern Center for Talent Development (CTD) -- 3-Week Academic Summer Camps

proposed_updates.citizenship_restrictions: CTD's eligibility model runs through standardized-test-score or talent-search thresholds rather than a nationality gate outright, and CTD explicitly names India, UAE, Kuwait, and Singapore as countries with a specific talent-search partner (ASSET) that maps to CTD's own admission tiers. Türkiye was not named among these specific partner countries in anything found this session -- meaning a Türkiye-based applicant's path in (via SAT/ACT/PSAT scores, or another accepted standardized measure) is plausible but not confirmed the way it is for the four named countries.
proposed_updates.residency_restrictions: CTD's own general international-student material states residential (in-person, on-campus) programs 'may have additional requirements for international participants, including visa considerations' -- unresolved specifics for this particular 3-week residential program.
proposed_updates.cost_currency_note: USD, unchanged from existing DB value, not re-verified this session.
proposed_updates.current_cycle_label: This program uses per-session deadlines one week before each session start; for the 2026 cycle, Session 1 closed June 21, 2026 and Session 2 closed August 1, 2026 -- both already elapsed as of this research (2026-08-26).

turkey_access_reasoning: CTD is confirmed to serve international students generally ('students from across the United States and internationally have participated'), but the specific admission pathway (standardized test score threshold via SAT/ACT/PSAT, since Türkiye is not one of the four countries with a named local talent-search partner) and the visa/logistics requirements for this specific RESIDENTIAL 3-week program are not fully confirmed for a Türkiye-based applicant -- real access likely exists but through a less-clearly-marked route than for the four explicitly-named partner countries, hence conditions rather than unconditional eligibility.

evidence.claim: International participation with visa caveat for residential programs
evidence.quote: Students from across the United States and internationally have participated in CTD programs...International students can apply to Northwestern CTD online programs. Residential programs on the Northwestern campus may have additional requirements for international participants, including visa considerations.
students from India, UAE, Kuwait or Singapore who have tested with ASSET Talent Search qualify for Indigo Tier programs with scores of 90th percentile or higher
The deadline for each session is one week before the start date...Session 1 [[deadline]] June 21, 2026...Session 2 [[deadline]] August 1, 2026

notes: Worth a follow-up: confirm whether a Türkiye-based applicant without an ASSET score can qualify via SAT/ACT/PSAT alone, and what CTD's actual visa process looks like for a 3-week residential stay (a B-2/short-term visa question, not resolved here).

title: UWC Short Courses
organizer: United World Colleges (UWC) -- individual short courses are organized independently by different UWC national committees/colleges
host_institution: Varies by course -- different UWC colleges/national committees worldwide

proposed_updates.citizenship_restrictions: General policy: 'Most courses welcome applications from all nationalities. However, some have regional focus or language requirements' -- this row is itself an UMBRELLA over many independently-organized short courses, each with its own specific eligibility, age range, cost, and deadline set by its own organizer.
proposed_updates.cost_currency_note: Varies by individual course -- one historical example found this session (a Türkiye-hosted 'Connecting Borders' course, see notes) charged EUR 600 (subsidized, national-committee-nominated) or EUR 700 (unsubsidized, independent candidates), but this specific course's page is stale (last-referenced application-open date was 2018) and should NOT be treated as currently running.
proposed_updates.current_cycle_label: Applications for individual courses are managed separately by each course's own organizer with its own timeline -- no single umbrella deadline exists.

turkey_access_reasoning: UWC's core mission is explicitly international/multi-nationality, and the general policy text confirms most individual courses welcome all nationalities. This is a genuine umbrella row (Contract's own umbrella-row concept), not a single program -- resolving Turkey-access at the general-policy level is reasonable, but a student should still check each specific course's own regional-focus/language requirements via the short-courses directory before assuming any given course is open.

evidence.quote: Most courses welcome applications from all nationalities. However, some have regional focus or language requirements. [...] Applications for UWC short courses are managed individually by course organisers.

notes: INTERESTING DEAD END, recorded for the next researcher's benefit rather than silently dropped: found a UWC short course literally titled 'Connecting Borders,' hosted IN Türkiye, open to ages 16-18 from 'Europe and the Middle East' (short-course-turkey.uwc.org/faq) -- but the page's only dated reference is 'Applications will open on 15th March, 2018,' with no evidence of a current or recent recurrence found this session. NOT presented as a current opportunity -- flagging only so a future pass knows this specific Türkiye-hosted course existed at some point and can check UWC's current short-courses directory for whether it (or something like it) has been revived, rather than re-discovering the same stale page from scratch.
